extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), the Office of Apprenticeship (OA), and stakeholders submitting public comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for registering and operating Department of Labor registered apprenticeship programs, including occupation determinations, data collection/reporting, program registration requirements, CTE apprenticeship projections, and associated compliance burdens and cost estimates. Intended to instruct sponsors, SAAs, OA, and employers on what the proposed rule requires and how impacts were estimated.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards for Apprenticeship and National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines “National Program Standards for Apprenticeship” and “National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards” to promote innovation and enable ease of access to industry-recognized, standardized products intended to facilitate expansion of new quality programs to be registered expeditiously and efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These national products create a more efficient process for approval of National Program Standards and for local registration of National Guidelines. They are intended as standardized templates that sponsors or SAAs can leverage to save time and costs when registering programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a national system of occupational frameworks that incentivize quality in registered apprenticeship programs and feature industry-validated training standards and curricula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Occupational Standards provide templates for national occupations, programs, and guidelines; they are to be continuously reinforced and improved with validated industry feedback, and can be leveraged by sponsors/SAAs instead of submitting new occupation determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints procedures and apprentice identity protections (§29.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would extend the amount of time for apprentices to file complaints against sponsors and would provide requirements that Registration Agencies better protect the identity of apprentices who file complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer filing windows and identity protections are expected to increase apprentices' comfort in filing complaints, potentially improving work conditions and completion rates. Registration Agencies must implement protections for complainant identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration process and suspension step (§29.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a suspension step allowing sponsors time to update practices and come into compliance without being deregistered and needing to reregister later; a Registration Agency would suspend registration of new apprentices until compliance via voluntary compliance action plan or until final order in deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is an intermediary enforcement step intended to reduce the number of programs that fully deregister or voluntarily deactivate. Sponsors granted suspension should follow voluntary compliance action plans to regain full active registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory quantitative analysis conventions (time horizon, dollars, discount rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory analysis focuses on likely consequences over 10 years, expresses impacts in 2022 dollars, and uses discount rates of 3 and 7 percent, pursuant to OMB Circular A-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All monetized costs and benefits in the analysis use a 10-year analytic window, 2022-dollar normalization, and present results at 3% and 7% discount rates for sensitivity; public comment is requested on these analytic assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population projection methodology for programs/sponsors/employers/apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses historical data (EDP or RAPIDS) from 2017–2022 to calculate average annual increases (e.g., average annual increase in programs = 942; new programs average = 73) and applies those increments to project populations from 2025–2034. Assumes number of sponsors equals number of programs due to data limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections are built by averaging year-to-year differences and applying averages forward; where data are limited, assumptions (e.g., sponsor count = program count) are explicitly noted and the Department seeks comment on reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review frequency and agency review share
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registered apprenticeship program is reviewed every 5 years (20% reviewed annually). Of programs reviewed, 58.2% are reviewed by SAAs and 41.8% by OA (based on averages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentages are applied to projected program populations to determine expected annual review workloads for SAAs and OA and to estimate administrative burdens and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employers-per-program and apprentices-per-sponsor ratios used for projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Derives the number of participating employers by applying a ratio of roughly 1.53 employers per program (2022 RAPIDS data). For CTE and other projections, uses 1.53 employers per sponsor and 23.4 apprentices per sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fixed ratios are used to convert projected numbers of sponsors/programs into counts of participating employers and apprentices; the Department applies the ratios consistently across projection years but solicits comment on their appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: New and revised occupation application projection rules (§29.7 assumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses historical RAPIDS data (2019–2022) to estimate average annual new occupation applications (15). For revisions, because OA would review approved occupations every 5 years, the Department divides current approved occupations (~1,100) by 5 to get ~220 revised occupations per year. Also assumes 15 new national occupations yearly based on Apprenticeship.gov bulletin lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employs distinct assumptions for new vs. revised determinations and includes industry feedback steps under the proposed §29.7(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE SAA and CTE program adoption projection assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes half of States with recognized SAAs would become CTE SAAs by 2034; models a steady increase to 16 CTE SAAs by 2035 assuming 3% of remaining States enter each year (≈1 SAA/year). For CTE program sponsors, estimates potential sponsor pool from LEAs receiving Perkins funds and postsecondary institutions, then assumes small adoption rates (1% first year, 3% second year, 3% each subsequent year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit modeling assumptions intended for public comment; the Department notes the voluntary nature of CTE registration and requests input on the reasonableness of assumed adoption rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation rate calculation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses BLS mean hourly wage rates for private/state employees and OPM salary table for Federal employees, includes nonwage factors by applying occupation-specific fringe benefits rates (private 42%, State 62%, Federal 63%) and an overhead rate of 17%; hourly compensation = base wage + (base wage × fringe_rate) + (base wage × overhead_rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit tables show example calculations for positions (e.g., Training & Development Manager, Apprentice). These loaded hourly rates are used to monetize time burdens and cost estimates in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule familiarization burden (one-time) for sponsors, employers, and SAAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates one-time reading/review times when rule becomes final: sponsor Training & Development Manager 4 hours; participating employers Training & Development Manager 2 hours; each SAA Training & Development Manager 4 hours. Subsequent years apply only to new sponsors/employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates are based on prior RIAs and program experience; Department requests comment on time assumptions. Example cost calculations provided (e.g., year 1 sponsor cost = 26,492 sponsors × 4 hours × $103.10/hour).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-job training documentation requirement (§29.7(b)(3)) — 2,000 hour minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must submit documentation of the industry standard of minimum hours needed to obtain proficiency in the occupation under consideration, and that the minimum hours are not less than 2,000 hours. Programs not meeting the 2,000-hour minimum must update their OJT requirements and submit documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates sponsors would spend 8 hours updating OJT requirements and 2 hours submitting documentation per affected occupation; applies to competency-based and hybrid programs that currently have <2,000 hours OJT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage analysis and career development profile documentation (§29.7(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must submit documentation of the typical compensation and career advancement profile for each occupation that places workers in an occupation that leads to a sustainable career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates 2 hours per existing/new/revised occupation for a sponsor's Training & Development Manager to develop and submit this documentation; aligns with prior IRAP RIA time estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOL-OA occupation determination evaluation process (§29.7(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: OA's process for evaluating occupation determinations is updated to be more precise about what is evaluated (including new documentation under §29.7(b)) and formalizes soliciting feedback from industry leaders on suitability of occupations for registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costing assumptions: OA GS-13 manager spends an additional 4 hours per occupation application reviewing new documentation; industry leaders spend ~2 hours providing feedback. The Department seeks comment on these time assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice-level data collection elements (§29.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed apprentice-level data collections include pre-apprenticeship services, occupations, and wage schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most data elements are expected to be dropdowns or choice answers (like current ETA-671) and are estimated to take apprentices ~5 minutes (0.083 hours) to provide; Department seeks comment on time estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor-level data collection elements (§29.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed sponsor-level data collections include participating employers, copies of program standards adoption agreements, participation with credentialing agencies, numbers of new and active apprentices, completed apprentices, out-of-pocket costs by apprentices, and earnings from completed apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors are estimated to require a Training & Development Manager 0.33 hours to provide standards info, and office/admin support 0.083 hours per apprentice and per participating employer to provide additional data. These are model inputs for burden and cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship written requirements (§29.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates requirements for the written set of standards of apprenticeship to include information on term of the apprenticeship program and related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must ensure standards documentation includes specified elements; estimated time burden for sponsors to update these standards is included in the RIA (0.33 hour per sponsor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement content and delivery requirements (§29.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must give the signed apprenticeship agreement to the apprentice and include new information in the apprenticeship agreements such as descriptions of roles, terms and conditions, end-point assessments, unreimbursed costs/expenses/fees, and credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors are estimated to spend 0.083 hours per apprentice providing the apprenticeship agreement and associated information. The rule formalizes delivery and content obligations to increase transparency for apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration application additional information (§29.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: New program registration applications must include additional information: a narrative on how the sponsor is working with the workforce system, information on financial capacity and other resources to operate the proposed program, and any history of violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors are estimated to spend 1 hour (Training & Development Manager) submitting the additional information for new program applications. Registration Agencies (SAAs/OA) must review these additions (estimated 0.5 hours per reviewing manager), and time/costs are included in RIA estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reporting burden assumptions for SAAs and sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: To transmit the new data collections to OA, SAAs are estimated to have a Training & Development Manager spend 1.5 hours per sponsor; sponsors estimated burdens include T&D manager time for standards and office/admin time for per-apprentice and per-employer entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These time assumptions are used to compute annualized costs (e.g., SAAs year 1 cost = 26,492 sponsors × 1.5 hours × $74.25/hour). The Department seeks public comment on these burden assumptions.
